fixes.title: Fix Local Signals: Waterdown + Mortgage Broker everywhere
fixes.whyItMatters: Your local visibility score is very low (20). Instagram discovery for local intent depends on clear category + city signals in high-weight fields like name, captions, and geotags.
fixes.exactAction: Update the account name field to include location and category (example: "Jelinek Mortgages | Waterdown Mortgage Broker"). Then, for the next 10 posts: add “Waterdown” and “mortgage broker” in the first 2 lines of each caption and tag the location “Waterdown, ON” on every post.
fixes.evidence: Local visibility score is 20 and the only checked term shown is “waterdown, ontario”.

fixes.title: Install a single clear pre-approval CTA + link path on every post
fixes.whyItMatters: Sales readiness is middling (48) with only 12/50. Mortgage audiences need an obvious next step and a clear route through your Linktree to reduce drop-off.
fixes.exactAction: Add one explicit line at the end of every post caption in a consistent format: "For help with a pre-approval in Waterdown, use the link in bio." Then, inside Linktree, ensure the top link is labeled exactly "Pre-approval (Waterdown)" and points to the intended landing page/form.
fixes.evidence: Sales readiness score is 48 and evidence shows 12/50; website is a Linktree, so the missing piece is an obvious CTA and link path.

fixes.title: A/B test your Link-in-bio destination using pinned posts
fixes.whyItMatters: Profile conversion is strong (70), meaning visitors are already interested—but the next step (your Linktree path) may not be converting at the highest rate. A/B testing reduces guesswork.
fixes.exactAction: Create two pinned posts: Pin A uses a caption centered on "Residential mortgages" and ends with "Use the link in bio for residential help in Waterdown." Pin B centers on "Investment & commercial mortgages" and ends with the same CTA wording. In Linktree, make the first two links match these exact intents (e.g., "Residential help (Waterdown)" and "Investment/Commercial help (Waterdown)"). Over 14 days, keep Pin A live on half the time by swapping pins weekly, and compare which pin gets more profile clicks.
fixes.evidence: Profile conversion score is 70 and the nextMove in the data is to A/B test link-in-bio and pinned posts.

fixes.title: Standardize a signature “Waterdown mortgage scenarios” carousel format
fixes.whyItMatters: Content performance shows a problem signal (55, with 0.00% across 0 posts). Even if that’s a reporting artifact, the leverage move is to produce a repeatable, save/share-friendly format tailored to local needs.
fixes.exactAction: For your next 6 posts, publish only carousels using this template: Slide 1: “Waterdown mortgage scenarios (quick answers)”. Slide 2: “Scenario: First-time buyer in Waterdown” (1-line situation). Slide 3: “What to ask your broker” (3 bullet questions). Slide 4: “Common pitfalls” (2 bullets). Slide 5: “What info we’ll need” (3 bullets). Slide 6: “Next step: pre-approval support via link in bio.” Keep the caption first line: “Waterdown mortgage broker: …” and include “Waterdown” in the caption and geotag.
fixes.evidence: Content performance score is 55 and Competitor gap is 97, so a repeatable signature format can differentiate while also improving saves/shares.

fixes.title: Differentiate against competitors with a “Broker knowledge” series (licensing + depth)
fixes.whyItMatters: Competitor gap is very favorable (97), but you still need visible differentiation in the feed. Your bio already signals “Trusted experience and in-depth industry knowledge,” so turn that into a recognizable series competitors don’t typically structure.
fixes.exactAction: Start a weekly series called: “Broker License Insights (Broker #13324)”. Create one post per week for 4 weeks using the same structure: (1) a licensing/eligibility misconception, (2) the corrected explanation in plain language, (3) 2 “questions to ask” prompts for Waterdown borrowers, (4) CTA line: “For pre-approval help, use the link in bio.”
fixes.evidence: Competitor gap score is 97 with nextMove to differentiate with a signature format competitors don’t use.

hookFormulas: If you’re buying a home in Waterdown and you’re unsure about {mortgage topic}, this is for you.
Stop guessing: {common mortgage mistake} is why many Waterdown buyers get surprised at closing.
Waterdown homeowners: before you renew your mortgage, check {key decision point}.
You don’t need perfect credit to get help—here’s what matters most for {mortgage topic}.
One thing lenders care about that most people miss: {factor} (Waterdown edition).
Investment property in Waterdown? Here’s the practical difference between {two loan types}.
Commercial mortgage basics for Waterdown business owners: {simplified concept}.
The fastest way to avoid delays on a mortgage in Waterdown is {process step}.
Before you switch mortgage brokers in Waterdown, verify {checklist item}.
I see this every week with residential/investment/commercial clients in Waterdown: {problem}.
What your mortgage rate actually depends on: {3–4 factors}.
ctaOptions: Use the link in bio to explore mortgage support options.
Visit the Linktree in bio for resources and next steps.
Download/Review options via the link in bio.
For personalized guidance for Waterdown residential, investment, or commercial mortgages, use the link in bio to get started.
reelIdeas: “Waterdown mortgage rates: what actually affects your rate?” (30–45s, quick bullets on factors to ask about)
“Pre-approval vs approval—what’s the difference?” (explain for Waterdown buyers, highlight timelines and what documents matter)
“Renewal mistakes Waterdown homeowners make” (arm yourself with 3 things to review before renewal)
“Investment property mortgage: 3 practical questions to ask” (cash flow, down payment considerations, rental income treatment—kept general)
“Commercial mortgage 101 for Waterdown business owners” (what lenders typically look for; keep it high-level)
“How to avoid mortgage delays in Waterdown” (document readiness + communication + timeline planning)
“What’s included in a typical mortgage application package?” (walkthrough-style, general list)
“Should you refinance? Here’s how to think about it” (frame as decision questions: rate, term, goals—no promises)
“Condo / rental / residential—what changes?” (compare at a high level and what to confirm)
carouselIdeas: Waterdown Mortgage Options: Residential vs Investment vs Commercial (who it’s for + what to consider)
Pre-Approval Checklist for Waterdown Buyers (documents + timeline + next steps)
Mortgage Renewal Prep (what to review 90 days before renewal—general checklist)
Top 10 Questions to Ask Your Mortgage Broker (tailor sections: residential, investment, commercial)
Common Mortgage Myths (Waterdown edition) + what’s true instead
“Your Mortgage Payment Breakdown” (principal/interest + factors that influence changes—kept conceptual)
Down Payment Planning for First-Time Buyers in Waterdown (decision framework, not exact rates)
Refinance Decision Framework (when it helps, when to pause, what to compare)
proofIdeas: Showcase your professionalism: post a carousel titled “Broker Lic #13324 — What it means for clients” (education-focused, no claims beyond the license).
Client journey-style content: “From first questions to funding—what the process usually looks like” (keep generic; no personal data).
Educational proof: “What I review for Waterdown residential, investment, and commercial borrowers” (create a framework that demonstrates expertise).
Authority posts: “What industry knowledge looks like—how I compare options for different scenarios” (process-based proof).
Trust-building Reel: “How to prepare for your mortgage conversation” (demonstrates readiness and care; invite viewers to use link in bio).
